meta.title: The Experience Economy
meta.topic: Malls adding art and sports instead of just retail.

Listen to a presentation by Dr. Elena Moss on 'The Neurobiology of Memories'. Complete the notes. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)
Listen to a panel discussion on 'The Post-Retail World'. Complete the table. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)
Listen to the steering committee debate on 'Cultural Capital'. Complete the matrix. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Hong Kong Diploma of Secondary Education Examination 2026. English Language Paper 3. Listening and Integrated Skills. The Experience Economy - High Stamina Mock Exam. This examination is specifically designed to test your absolute focus, long-term resilience, and high-speed information processing over an extended listening duration. This recording will be played once only and contains no pauses other than those officially stated in the instructions. Candidates are reminded that accuracy in capturing technical details is vital for Level 5 success.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: The entire broadcast will last approximately one hour and thirty minutes. During the examination, you will hear several recordings. You will have time to read the instructions and the questions. You will also have time to check your work. Please ensure your electronic devices are switched off and placed under your chair in the provided signal-blocking bags. If you have any problems with the volume or clarity of the broadcast, please inform the supervisor immediately. Part A. Task 1. You are at the registration desk for 'The Experience Economy Expo 2026'. Listen to the conversation between the receptionist, Sarah, and an event planner, Alex Vance. Complete the registration and technical survey form. You now have two minutes to study the task. During these two minutes, you should familiarize yourself with the form structure and the specific data points required, such as the contact details, equipment models, and specific dietary requirements for the group. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Good morning! Welcome to the 2026 Experience Economy Expo. We are currently in the absolute peak registration hour of the first day, and as you can probably see from the massive crowd at the lanyard station, the biometric scanners, and the digital check-in kiosks, things are getting quite intense and crowded back here in the main hall! We have over four hundred experiential brands here today, representing everything from immersive theater and sensory-sync gaming to neuro-responsive dining and holographic retail. It's officially the largest event of its kind in Southeast Asia, and we’re expecting over fifteen thousand industry professionals, investors, and tech enthusiasts over the next three days. It’s a massive logistical challenge, but we’re making sure every detail is perfect for our high-profile guests. How can I assist you with your check-in and technical registration this morning? Are you here as an individual attendee or representing a corporate group?

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Good morning, Sarah. I can certainly feel the 'Experience' and the high energy already! I've been in the security queue for nearly twenty-five minutes just to get past the initial biometric gate and the thermal scanners. My name is Alex Vance—that's A-L-E-X, and Vance is V-A-N-C-E. I'm the lead planner for Global Mall Solutions. We have a major presentation later today in the innovation track regarding the future of sensory malls, and we’re also running several live demonstrations in the main sensory hall, so I hope our logistics and technical requirements are fully synchronized in your system for the Diamond tier.

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Global Mall Solutions... let me just look that up on our main experiential portal server. The system is being a bit laggy this morning, probably because every single exhibitor is trying to download the high-resolution AR navigation maps and the real-time attendee tracking dashboard at the same time. Ah, yes, here you are. Alex Vance. And I have your primary contact number listed as 9876 1234. Is that still the best direct mobile line to reach you if we have any last-minute shifts in the breakout schedule or if your high-frequency VR equipment interferes with the hall’s sensory-sync network again? We really can't have another technical blackout like the one in Tokyo last year.

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: 9-8-7-6, 1-2-3-4. Yes, that's my direct mobile number, and I can promise our new transmitters are much more stable and frequency-isolated this year! And I see we've been confirmed for the 'Diamond Executive' tier for the 2026 Expo. That should include the priority access to the sensory lounges, the VIP briefing in the Grand Atrium, and the executive parking passes for our tech transport team, correct? Our board members were very specific about the networking benefits of that tier when they approved the budget for this event.

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Diamond Executive. Correct. It’s our top-tier corporate membership for the 2026 Expo. Now, I need to confirm the final staff badge count for your group. My records say you requested ten badges back in February, but I see a flagged update here from your office regarding a last-minute increase for your design team and the senior interns.

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Yes, we actually increased our team to fourteen attendees in total. We've brought the entire design department from our new West Kowloon project because the keynote on 'Sensory Branding' is absolutely vital for their current design phase. We need all fourteen badges to have full-access permissions, including the behind-the-scenes tour of the immersive stage and the executive lunch area. It’s a massive learning opportunity for the junior designers and we want them to see the tech in action without any restrictions.

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Fourteen badges. Noted. I’ll print the extra four for you right now—it’ll just take a moment for the high-res thermal printer to warm up. Your team has been assigned the Grand Atrium Hall for your private consultation and technical briefing sessions. It's the largest space we have in the venue, right under the central glass dome, so you’ll have plenty of space for your prototypes and the massive sensory screens. Now, for your technical requirements—how many VR headsets are you renting from our tech pool today?

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: We need exactly three VR headsets. We're running a live demo of our new 'Virtual Store Walkthrough' model, and we want to rotate our designers and potential investors through it in small, controlled groups throughout the afternoon. We also need high-bandwidth 6G connectivity for the live cloud-rendering demo that syncs with our main servers in London. If the connectivity drops or lags, the whole immersive experience falls apart and it looks very unprofessional to our VIP stakeholders.

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Three VR headsets and 6G priority. Done. I’ll make sure the tech team gives you the dedicated router password for the Atrium zone. Now, regarding the catering for your staff group... I have a note here about a specific dietary restriction for the Global group. Is it a vegan requirement for the whole team, or just the project leads?

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: No, it's a severe nut allergy. One of our senior architects is highly sensitive to all types of nuts—peanuts, cashews, even almonds or walnuts. It's a critical safety issue, so the catering for our entire group of fourteen must be strictly nut-free for the lunch buffet. We can’t have any risk of cross-contamination in the VIP dining area, as it would be an absolute disaster. Please ensure the catering manager and the floor supervisor are personally informed about this today.

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Strictly Nut-free. I’ve tagged that in bright red on the catering manifest for the Diamond hall. Which afternoon workshop did the team finally decide on? You were torn between 'Gourmet Food Courts' and 'Sports Hub Design' for a while.

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: We've finally gone with Sports Hub Design. It’s much more relevant to our 'Project Playground' initiative and our shift towards wellness-based retail experiences. Lastly, for the billing and invoicing—can you make sure the address is listed as Central Plaza Tower 2? Our finance team in West Kowloon won't process the payment if it’s not the main headquarters address clearly visible on the receipt.

script.speaker: Sarah
script.text: Central Plaza Tower 2. Perfect. And I see the registration fee status is already marked as 'Paid' via the corporate account bank transfer from last Friday. Here are your badges, your VIP handbook, and your sensory-sync devices, Alex. Have a productive, immersive, and successful expo! I hope those VR headsets behave themselves and don't cause any motion sickness this year.

script.speaker: Alex
script.text: Thanks, Sarah! I’m sure they’ll be fine. We’ve upgraded the frame rate to 120Hz. See you around the hall.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 2. Listen to a presentation by Dr. Elena Moss on 'The Neurobiology of Memories'. Complete the notes. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Dr. Elena Moss
script.text: Good morning, colleagues, students, and visionaries of the 2026 Experience Economy. In the current era, we no longer talk about 'buying things' or 'acquiring physical products' in the traditional sense. We talk about 'buying memories,' 'acquiring identity,' and 'investing in the experiential self.' We first brainstormed the concept of 'Project Playground' back in 2022 when we realized that traditional, transactional retail alone was no longer a viable draw for younger, experience-hungry crowds who value digital capital and social status over material clutter. Our pilot mall, 'The Sky-Hub Mall' in East Kowloon, was the first to undergo a total transformation from a static, boring shopping center to a dynamic, ever-changing 'Immersive Ecosystem'. Instead of another department store or a generic food court, we installed a massive 15-meter Indoor Bouldering wall right in the central atrium, surrounded by interactive light displays and neuro-responsive soundscapes. In the first quarter of operations, we saw a staggering footfall increase of 22%. Our primary target demographic is Gen-Z professionals—those who value 'experience capital' and social sharing over material ownership. We dedicated exactly 10,000 square feet to these high-energy sports and sensory facilities, creating a hub that feels alive twenty-four hours a day.

script.speaker: Dr. Elena Moss
script.text: I want to share a case study from our Tokyo partner mall. There, they implemented the 'Sensory Echo' module, where shoppers' movements are translated into live digital art that is projected onto the mall exterior. This created a 'FOMO' effect—Fear Of Missing Out—that drove traffic up by another 15% in just six weeks. This is the neurobiology of awe in action. While the initial build for such projects was a massive investment in the future of our brand, the main recurring cost is the annual insurance, which now totals $1.2 Million due to the high-risk nature of the climbing walls and the new 'Extreme Empathy' sensory modules that we’ve integrated into the immersive yoga studios. Our construction partner for this, Apex Build Corp, handled the structural reinforcement and the acoustic dampening perfectly. We are now preparing for our official member-only launch on August 15, which is already sold out. The core of our success is the dopamine spike—we’ve found through neuro-mapping that immersive environments increase memory retention by 40% compared to traditional browsing. The Experience Market Cap in Hong Kong is projected to hit $800 Million by the end of this year, driven by this massive shift in consumer psychology. Our next digital feature is the 'Digital Skate Park' which uses LIDAR sensors to track movement in real-time. For any technical inquiries, please email us at info@project-p.hk. We’ll also be hosting a site tour at our Kwun Tong Annex next Friday for those interested in the backend tech. Join us in redesigning the reality of consumption and human connection.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 3. Listen to a panel discussion on 'The Post-Retail World'. Complete the table. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Host
script.text: Welcome to 'The Future of Commerce'. I'm your host, and today we're tackling the massive shift from storefronts to 'storyfronts'. Joining me are Dr. Lam, an urbanist; Ms. Gomez, an art consultant; and Mr. Tan, a retail developer. Dr. Lam, you've seen the data. Why are malls suddenly becoming art galleries and immersive theaters?

script.speaker: Dr. Lam
script.text: It's simple: online shopping has won the convenience war. People buy their essentials on their phones. Malls must now offer what the internet cannot—a physical, emotional, and social experience. Art provides those 'Instagrammable' moments that drive organic foot traffic and communal belonging. We're seeing a shift where art is no longer just a decoration, but the main anchor tenant that defines the mall’s brand identity. To manage this at scale, we have a new exhibition app called 'Art-Walk-HK'. It's fully trilingual—Cantonese, English, and Mandarin—which is absolutely essential for our international visitor base. Most of our pieces are 'Digital Installations' because they have high visual impact with a much smaller physical footprint than traditional sculpture. We also have over twenty-five locations currently signed up for the pilot phase.

script.speaker: Ms. Gomez
script.text: I agree, Dr. Lam, but malls often treat art like wallpaper or a marketing gimmick. To do it right, they should hire full-time, professional curators to ensure the narrative is cohesive and culturally resonant. We've set a grant application deadline of October 31 for artists who want to join our 'Sensory Hub' program. We're offering a subsidy cap of $45,000 per artist to cover materials, tech, and installation costs. We’ve also introduced 'Analog Points'—rewards for people who put their phones away in our 'Digital Detox' zones for at least thirty minutes. It’s about being truly present in the moment and reconnecting with the physical self.

script.speaker: Mr. Tan
script.text: The biggest hurdle is always the cost for the consumer. I believe we should have zero admission fees for these mall-based galleries. The mall makes its profit from the increased coffee, high-end dining, and luxury fashion sales driven by the traffic, so the art should be a free magnet for the community. Our lead corporate sponsor, Heritage Bank, has agreed to keep the commission rate at a low 10% for any art sold on-site to support local talent. If you have feedback or want to apply for a grant, please call 2100 3300. We're here to help the creative class thrive in this new Experience Economy.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Task 4. Listen to the steering committee debate on 'Cultural Capital'. Complete the matrix. You now have two minutes to study the task. (120-second pause)

script.speaker: Clara Li
script.text: As the owner of a luxury boutique specializing in high-end jewelry and vintage watches, I have to be brutally blunt with this committee today. The noise from the basketball court and the climbing wall next door is too disruptive for my retail experience. My VIP clients expect a quiet, sophisticated, and high-end environment to make their significant purchases. If the mall continues with this 'noisy' sports strategy on the main levels, my store's profit and brand reputation will suffer. I’m proposing that my rent should be lowered significantly to compensate for the lost atmosphere and the disruption. At the very least, they should restrict these high-decibel sports and sensory hubs to the roof level or the basement, far away from the 'Luxury Row' where the real spending happens and where my clients feel safe.

script.speaker: Artist
script.text: As a resident artist who uses the 'Extreme Empathy' modules, I see it from a completely different perspective. The noise and the movement create an energetic, vibrant, and alive atmosphere that makes the mall feel like a community hub rather than a sterile warehouse. The facilities and the grant support provided are fair given the quality of the tech and the high foot traffic. I actually think we should expand to group classes, live immersive theater, and interactive art in the common atriums to further engage the public and break down the walls between art and life. We need more energy, not less, to survive this digital age.

script.speaker: Manager
script.text: We have to find a sustainable balance for everyone involved. I've looked into high-density acoustic paneling and active sound-masking technology to dampen the sound near the luxury shops without killing the energetic vibe of the atrium. As for rent, we might move to a variable model based on peak sensory hours. But one thing we all agree on is safety—we must have mandatory medical clearance for anyone using the high-intensity sensory zones or the climbing walls. To incentivize shops like Clara’s to stay, we are introducing 'Heritage Preservation Credits'—a significant tax break and subsidy for those who integrate local art into their storefronts. We’ll also extend operating hours until 11 PM daily to capture the after-work crowd. We've also installed 'Anti-Slip Flooring' throughout the zones for everyone’s safety. Our next policy review is scheduled for January 2027. We’re moving towards 'Retail Therapy 2.0'. Meeting adjourned. Thank you for your input.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: This is the end of Part A. Now, turn to Part B.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: Part B. Introduction. You are Chris Wong, a project assistant at the Bureau of Cultural Affairs. You will hear a briefing given by the Bureau Chief to the implementation team. As you listen, take notes which may help you to complete the tasks. You will have five minutes to study the Part B Information Directory and the tasks. (Pause 5m)

script.speaker: Bureau Chief
script.text: Good morning, team. We have a lot of moving parts for the Q3 'Experience Economy' rollout, and the public scrutiny is higher than it’s ever been. Chris, make sure you capture these specific details for the upcoming tasks, as they are critical for our stakeholder management and public relations. First, addressing the vocal complaints from Clara Li and the Boutique owners. We are investigating the acoustic paneling solutions, but as a proactive step to build goodwill and long-term cooperation, I want you to officially announce the 'Heritage Preservation Credits' program in your response to her. This is a $20,000 tax break and design grant for shops that integrate local art into their storefront displays. It wasn't in the original policy draft, so it’s a vital 'Audio-Only' update that she needs to hear about today. It shows we’re rewarding them for their cooperation and helping them upgrade their brand.

script.speaker: Bureau Chief
script.text: Secondly, I want to address the 2024 E-commerce Logistics Roster that's been circulating in some of the local business forums and WhatsApp groups. PLEASE DISREGARD IT COMPLETELY. That report is two years old and focused entirely on physical warehouse efficiency, shipping fleets, and logistics in Wan Chai. It has absolutely nothing to do with our 2026 intangible experience-based strategy or the shift towards memory-based consumption. If any tenants, activists, or students try to cite the 98% delivery efficiency as a reason to stick to traditional transactional retail, remind them that it's outdated and completely irrelevant data in the current experience economy. We are focusing strictly on the new 2026 sensory-based stats from 'The Sky-Hub'. Don’t let them derail our progress with archive noise.

script.speaker: Bureau Chief
script.text: For our summer outreach campaign, I want to use the new 'Digital Skate Park' facility to launch a 'Summer Skate Jam' festival in August. It’s a great way to boost the footfall gap we usually see during the extreme summer heatwaves. This event is a specific detail for the internal marketing memo, so don't miss it. We also need to highlight that our partner, Apex Build Corp, has secured the new international safety certification, which is why we’ve installed 'Anti-Slip Flooring' throughout the sports and sensory zones. This is a key safety feature for our elderly visitors and families that we need to promote heavily in our social media campaign to reassure the public.

script.speaker: Bureau Chief
script.text: Lastly, for the social media post for our 'Active Life' membership, use the specific campaign catchphrase 'Retail Therapy 2.0'. It frames the experience and the physical activity alongside the psychological and emotional benefits of the modern mall. Chris, I want the drafts for the letter to Clara, the internal memo to the Marketing Director, and the social media post on my desk by 5:00 PM today. We have a real chance to redefine the Hong Kong mall experience and prove that physical spaces still matter in a digital world. Let’s make it count. Alright, everyone, back to work.

script.speaker: Announcer
script.text: That is the end of the Integrated Skills recording. You now have 1 hour and 15 minutes to complete your tasks. (End of simulation)
